title.narrative: Activity under preparation Promoting Opportunities With Energy Resilience ¿ Myanmar (POWER ¿ Myanmar)

description.narrative: Myanmar energy sector is severely hindered by a combination of prolonged underinvestment, policy mismanagement, the socioeconomic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic, recurrent natural disasters and ongoing conflict. These challenges have exacerbated existing vulnerabilities, resulting in chronic supply shortages, ageing infrastructure and an energy system incapable of meeting demand. Over forty per cent of rural areas remain entirely off grid, while those with connections face an unreliable supply that undermines livelihoods and essential service delivery.For rural communities, especially smallholder farmers and agrifood MSMEs, unreliable electricity continues to limit productivity and income generation. This is particularly critical in a sector that employs around half of the workforce and accounts for 20¿25% of GDP. The challenge is intensified by rising input costs, conflict-related transport disruptions and the continued exclusion of remote and conflict-affected areas from market opportunities. Many farmers and rural enterprises still depend on diesel generators, despite their high cost, pollution and unreliable fuel supply. Since March 2026, the Gulf war has further exposed Myanmar¿s energy vulnerability, leading to fuel restrictions, shortages and rising prices that are severely affecting agricultural value chains.This action will support a just transition to renewable energy in Myanmar¿s rural economy by strengthening the resilience of vulnerable rural communities and MSMEs and reducing energy poverty and economic vulnerability. It will help smallholders and MSMEs shift from costly, carbon-intensive energy sources to affordable, decentralised renewable solutions, while expanding access to electricity in selected rural areas through mini-grids and, where these are not viable, tailored off-grid systems. The action will also promote renewable energy for essential services, including water and sanitation, healthcare, education and ICT, improve the uptake of energy-efficient and responsible technologies by rural MSMEs, and create green jobs through skills development, market linkages, TVET and practical training for the installation, maintenance and repair of renewable energy systems.The programme will deliver efficient and sustainable sources of renewable electricity for off-grid and underserved rural areas, enhancing access to basic services and increasing the number of rural MSMEs adopting energy-efficient practices. It will also build local capacity and create green employment opportunities for individuals, contributing to broader economic and social resilience.Solar energy is the most practical option under current conditions. For rural MSMEs and smallholders, both diesel and grid electricity are costly and unreliable, while solar offers a more affordable investment with long-term savings. Solar micro- and mini-grids can also be managed locally, reducing reliance on centralised systems that are vulnerable to conflict and poor management. At community and MSME level, solar solutions provide a practical and autonomous alternative that directly benefits those most in need.By focusing on scalable, community-driven renewable energy, this action will mitigate immediate energy poverty while laying the foundation for long-term economic recovery and climate adaptation in Myanmar¿s rural areas.The proposed action aims to contribute to the priorities outlined in the amended Regional Multiannual Indicative Programme (MIP) for Asia and the Pacific (2021-2027), in particular the new section ¿1.3.4 ¿ Priority area 4 ¿ Actions in countries in complex settings¿.
